name: Ethena LayerZero OFTAdapters

requirements.label: Admin power is not a bare key
A confirmed delay before changes apply, no bypass
Bypass paths of the delay checked and ruled out
Price feed not under one hand
No key shared with another tracked protocol

exit_window: a delay with a bypass, or one not ruled out

narrative.summary: Same EthenaTimelockController as the PSM above governs all three cross-chain bridges - but here the bypassable function is setPeer(), which redirects the trusted remote counterpart.
narrative.tag: more severe than the PSM’s gap
narrative.detail: setPeer(uint32,bytes32) is confirmed whitelisted (instant bypass) on all three adapters - a compromised executor could point a peer at a malicious remote contract and mint/redeem against a fake bridge, not merely freeze activity. setDelegate() is confirmed genuinely delayed. USDe alone backs $5.14B on Ethereum; these adapters are the real cross-chain path for that value, not a side contract. This is exactly the risk class the KelpDAO $292M exploit (see the incident panel above) realized in production on a different protocol’s bridge.

steps.what: owner() on the contract: the holder
